epic.title: Unbranded Analysis and Other Prompts
epic.jiraSummary: EPIC-046: Unbranded Analysis and Other Prompts
epic.functionalNeed:
This epic opens GEO to analyses without a brand, and lets a prompt run without a category or a question type. An unbranded analysis measures an industry or a topic instead of a brand (football, car insurance, frozen food). The topic frames the analysis and is never measured: the measured entities are the brands the AI answers name. Everything set during creation stays manageable after launch in Manage Scope. An unbranded analysis stays unbranded: adding a brand to it comes in a later version.

It builds on the new-analysis wizard and the prompt pool of EPIC-034 (https://onclusive.atlassian.net/browse/GEO-1002). This epic adds a first step, Analysis Type, before Brand & Country, so the wizard has five steps: Analysis Type, Brand & Country (Topic & Country in an unbranded analysis), Categories, Prompts and Review. From step 1 onward a mode pill in the product bar reads Brand analysis or Unbranded analysis. An unbranded analysis consumes the pool exactly like a brand analysis. Both features ship behind one global flag, off until validated, then on for every organisation. While the flag is off, the wizard stays as it is today: four steps, no Analysis Type step and no mode pill.

A prompt that misses its category or its type falls back to Other instead of being blocked. It still runs and returns key concepts, which feed InBrief and Top Concepts (Top Topics in an unbranded analysis), and it moves to its category and type once classified. In EPIC-034 both are required.

The functional rules come from the GEO flexible scope behaviour spec (rule IDs such as S3.12 are quoted where useful). The design is the Figma page "Onboarding / New Analysis V3" of the Measure - GEO Module file: [https://www.figma.com/design/xctSRqtM653zRS7QY3KMm0/Measure---GEO-Module?node-id=13458-101707](https://www.figma.com/design/xctSRqtM653zRS7QY3KMm0/Measure---GEO-Module?node-id=13458-101707)

Every UI string of this epic, with its key and its en-US, en-GB, fr-FR and es-ES text, is in the strings sheet shared with EPIC-034. The criteria quote the English text only: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1G3C6DF1B_GmOrga4BB9GYtxv1fc-x7mCsnxyVsumL8Y/edit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1G3C6DF1B_GmOrga4BB9GYtxv1fc-x7mCsnxyVsumL8Y/edit)

stories.title: Run an analysis without a target brand

userStory.want: the topic to replace the brand everywhere the analysis needs a subject
userStory.so: the analysis runs and measures every brand the answers name

acceptanceCriteria.title: Mode and topic stored, no target
acceptanceCriteria.then: it stores its mode and topic with no target brand, and the topic is its name in the dashboard, emails and exports

acceptanceCriteria.title: No brand is the target
acceptanceCriteria.then: no brand is scored or treated as the target, brand grouping protects no target, and source classification receives the topic and the brands named

acceptanceCriteria.title: Topic split into 2 categories
acceptanceCriteria.then: the topic is split into 2 consumer search areas, such as "postal services" into "parcel delivery" and "international shipping", with no brand website

acceptanceCriteria.title: Production templates, [Competitor 4]
acceptanceCriteria.then: they use the 10 production templates of each type (frontend/src/utils/questionTemplates.ts): Visibility is unchanged and uses {category} only, and in Competitive the {entity} slot becomes [Competitor 4], so each competitive prompt compares the top 4 brands from that category and market's visibility answers

acceptanceCriteria.title: Adaptation with the topic
acceptanceCriteria.given: prompts are adapted and translated for a market
acceptanceCriteria.then: QUESTION_ADAPTATION receives the topic instead of the brand and drops the "entity must not appear" rule, and the topic does not have to appear in the text since the category already carries it

acceptanceCriteria.title: 10 Category Topics prompts per category
acceptanceCriteria.then: each category gets these 10, one per theme:
acceptanceCriteria.thenDetail:
| Theme | Prompt |
|---|---|
| Selection criteria | What should I look for in {category}? |
| Quality | What makes {category} good quality? |
| Price and value | What is good value for money in {category}? |
| Experience | What do people like most about {category}? |
| Problems | What are the most common problems with {category}? |
| Trust and safety | How do I know which {category} options I can trust? |
| Trends | What is changing in {category} right now? |
| Ethics and sustainability | What are the ethical and environmental concerns around {category}? |
| Expert advice | What do experts recommend about {category}? |
| Controversies | What are the main controversies in {category}? |

acceptanceCriteria.title: Category Topics questions run as written
acceptanceCriteria.then: they run as written without the Perception system instruction, like prompts with the Other type

acceptanceCriteria.title: Category Topics analysis
acceptanceCriteria.then: the Category Topics analysis prompt attached to GEO-1209 returns the topics raised, their sentiment for the category as a whole and up to 3 brands attached to each topic as written in the answers, on the non engine-native extraction path even when engine-native concepts are on

acceptanceCriteria.title: Competitive with too few competitors
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Competitive prompt of an unbranded analysis, outside the Other category
acceptanceCriteria.when: fewer than 2 competitors were extracted for its category and market
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is not sent for this run and shows no result in the prompts table. A brand analysis still sends it with the empty slots removed (Q7)
